claim: Section 5, unnumbered claim in α (hr part)
quote: Suppose random variables X and Y are distributed according to TEE(α1, λ1) and TEE(α2, λ2), respectively. If λ1 = λ2, then it is easy to show that g(x)/f(x) is a decreasing function of x if and only if α1 < α2. So, Y ⩽lr X implies Y ⩽hr X and hence we see that Y ⩽st X for α1 < α2.
compared: X ~ TEE(α1, λ) vs Y ~ TEE(α2, λ), common λ, α1 < α2

hypotheses.formal: equal rate parameter, ordered shape parameter

conclusion.direction: Y ≤hr X (larger-α variable smaller in hazard rate order)

claim: Section 5, unnumbered claim in λ (hr part)
quote: If α1 = α2 = α then g(x)/f(x) = (λ2/λ1)h(x), (8) where h(x) = e^{(λ1−λ2)x} e^{α(e^{−λ2 x}−e^{−λ1 x})}. Hence, we have ∂ log h(x)/∂x = q(λ1) − q(λ2), where q(λ) = λ(1 + αe^{−λx}). (9) It can be shown that if α > −1 then (9) is an increasing function of λ (see Appendix A for more details) and it follows that (8) is a decreasing function of x if λ1 < λ2. So, Y ⩽lr X implies Y ⩽hr X and hence we see that Y ⩽st X for any α > −1 and λ1 < λ2.
compared: X ~ TEE(α, λ1) vs Y ~ TEE(α, λ2), common α > −1, λ1 < λ2

hypotheses.text: α1 = α2 = α with α > −1; λ1 < λ2
hypotheses.formal: equal shape α > −1 (needed for q increasing in λ, Appendix A), ordered rates

conclusion.direction: Y ≤hr X (larger-λ variable smaller in hazard rate order)

adjudication: adjudicated: λ-claim prints Y ≤hr X under common α > −1 and λ1 < λ2.
